nodes.summary: If `m` is sufficient for a family of probability measures, every `m₀`-measurable real function `W` that is integrable under all the measures has one `m`-measurable version of the conditional expectation `P_θ[W | m]` for every `θ`. (Measurability of `W` itself, not only under each `P θ`, is what lets one approximating sequence serve every parameter.)
nodes.title: Common conditional expectation under a sufficient σ-algebra

nodes.summary: If the family of probability measures `P` is dominated by a σ-finite measure `μ` and the statistic `T` is sufficient for `P`, then the densities factor as `dP_θ/dμ = g_θ(T) · h` with measurable `g_θ` and `h`, `h` free of `θ`.
nodes.title: Halmos–Savage factorization, necessity

nodes.summary: If `T` is sufficient for `P`, then `P θ x = g θ (T x) * h x` with `g θ t = P_θ(T = t)` and a parameter-free `h` with values in `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Factorization, necessity

nodes.summary: Factorization criterion, sufficiency direction, for a statistic, under an extra σ-finiteness hypothesis. If `dP_θ/dμ = g_θ(T) · h` with `g_θ` and `h` measurable and `h · μ` σ-finite on the σ-algebra generated by `T`, then `T` is sufficient for `P`.
nodes.title: Factorization criterion, sufficiency direction, for a statistic, under an extra σ-finiteness hypothesis

nodes.summary: Factorization implies sufficiency (Halmos–Savage, the sufficiency half). If every `P θ` has a density `g θ` with respect to one measure `ν` that is σ-finite on `m`, and each `g θ` is `m`-measurable, then `m` is sufficient for `P`.
nodes.title: Factorization implies sufficiency

nodes.summary: The Fisher–Neyman factorization theorem (discrete case). A statistic `T` is sufficient for the family of mass functions `P` if and only if there are nonnegative functions `g` and `h`, with `h` free of the parameter, such that `P θ x = g θ (T x) * h x` for every `θ`, `x`.
nodes.title: The Fisher–Neyman factorization theorem

nodes.summary: If `P θ x = g θ (T x) * h x` for nonnegative real `g`, `h` with `h` free of `θ`, then `T` is sufficient for `P`.
nodes.title: Factorization, sufficiency

nodes.summary: A statistic `T : X → τ` is *sufficient* for the discrete family `P : Θ → PMF X` if the conditional probability `P θ x / P_θ(T = T x)` of `x` given `T = T x` is the same under any two parameters `θ, θ'` for which `{T = T x}` has positive probability. Here `P_θ(T = t) = (P θ).map T t`.
nodes.title: Sufficient statistic for a discrete family

nodes.summary: A sub-σ-algebra `m` is *sufficient* for the family of measures `P` on `(Ω, m₀)` if `m ≤ m₀`, every `P θ` is finite, and for every `m₀`-measurable set `s` one `m`-measurable function is a version of the conditional probability `P_θ[1_s | m]` under every `P θ`.
